This site collects the lecture slide decks, practical materials, and bibliography for the course.

## Course Abstract

This course introduces geospatial archaeology: how archaeologists represent,
measure, and analyse the locations of material traces, and how they move from
mapped patterns to defensible interpretations. It covers spatial data
(vector and raster), coordinate reference systems and projections, spatial
relationships and dependence, the fundamental GIS operations, and the effects of
scale, time, and the archaeological observation process on spatial patterns.
